ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A circular wooden board with a radius of \( r \) is stationary on the surface of a certain liquid. Directly below the center \( o \) of the circular board at a depth of \( H = \sqrt{3}r \), there is a point light source \( S \). The refractive index of the liquid is known to be \( n = \sqrt{2} \).

1. What is the angle of refraction of the refracted light ray exiting along the edge of the circular wooden board?
2. How much distance should the point source S be moved vertically upward so that the light emitted from S is just not visible above the water surface?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A circular wooden board with a radius of \( r \) is stationary on the surface of a certain liquid. Directly below the center \( O \) of the circular board at a depth of \( H = \sqrt{3}r \), there is a point light source \( S \). The refractive index of the liquid is \( n = \sqrt{2} \). 1. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the liquid surface is a horizontal line, and above the surface/against the surface there is a circular wooden board centered at O (drawn as a small horizontal board in the cross section), with the radius r marked from O to the edge of the wooden board. The point light source S is located directly below O, O and S are connected by a vertical dashed line, and the depth H is marked on the right with a vertical bracket. The illustrated structure shows that the light ray emitted along the edge of the wooden board corresponds to the ray from S striking the edge point of the liquid surface at a horizontal distance r from O. Reasoning: Take the edge ray from S toward the edge of the wooden board. Its angle of incidence i is the angle between the ray and the normal to the liquid surface (the vertical direction), so tan i = r/H. Given H = sqrt(3)r, tan i = r/(sqrt(3)r)=1/sqrt(3), giving i=30°. Light enters air from a liquid with refractive index n=sqrt(2). According to Snell's law, n sin i = sin theta, that is, sqrt(2) sin30° = sin theta = sqrt(2)/2, so theta=45°. If S is moved vertically upward and the new depth is h, in order for the light to be just invisible above the water surface, all rays that can reach the uncovered liquid surface should undergo total internal reflection. The uncovered liquid surface begins at the radius r at the edge of the wooden board; for these rays, the one with the smallest angle of incidence is the ray striking the edge of the wooden board. The critical angle C satisfies sin C = 1/n = 1/sqrt(2), so C=45°. When it is just invisible, set the angle of incidence of the edge ray equal to the critical angle: tan C = r/h. Since tan45°=1, r/h=1, h=r. The initial depth H=sqrt(3)r, so the required vertical upward displacement is H-h = sqrt(3)r-r = (sqrt(3)-1)r ≈ 0.73r.
